text:
maria: CI canary build is failing during the push step to our registry — `PUT /v2/redwood/app/manifests/...` returns 503 and the job shows `unexpected EOF` and `blob upload incomplete`. Job: https://ci.redwood.internal/1234
build-bot: [job 1234] stage=push status=FAILED log_excerpt=`PUT /v2/redwood/app/manifests/sha256:... 503 Service Unavailable
error: unexpected EOF while reading response`
jonathan: is this happening only on canary or on main too?
maria: only canary so far. Failure started after Dockerfile tweak in commit `9f3a7b2` (small change to multi-stage layering). Local `docker build` + push to my personal registry works. CI push fails consistently on that job.
sara: could be a corrupted cache layer on the builder pool or a transient registry flake. Quick checks: try a no-cache build or disable kaniko cache: `docker build --no-cache -t ... .` or `--cache=false` for kaniko. Also inspect the manifest with `skopeo inspect docker://registry.redwood/internal/app:canary`.
liam: also worth trying `docker pull registry.redwood/internal/app:canary` from a build node to ensure manifests/layers are reachable. If manifest exists but blob upload is failing, registry might be rejecting chunked uploads.
maria: ran `skopeo inspect` from my laptop, manifest looks fine. Short log snippet from CI (push step):
```
PUT /v2/redwood/app/blobs/uploads/uuid HTTP/1.1 202 Accepted
PATCH /v2/redwood/app/blobs/uploads/uuid HTTP/1.1 201 Created
POST /v2/redwood/app/manifests/sha256:... HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
error: unexpected EOF while reading response
```
jonathan: thanks. Can you trigger a CI rerun with forced rebuild (no cache)? If it still fails we should bisect commits between last-green and this break. Add a `CI_FORCE_REBUILD=true` env and rerun.
maria: queued rerun with `CI_FORCE_REBUILD=true` (link: https://ci.redwood.internal/1234/retry)
alex: if rerun still fails I can run a bisect locally. Post the commit range (last green commit sha + current sha) and I’ll try stepping through Dockerfile diffs. Also consider clearing buildkit state on builder nodes: `sudo systemctl stop buildkit && sudo rm -rf /var/lib/buildkit/* && sudo systemctl start buildkit` — only do during low traffic.
sara: also suggest adding a small retry wrapper around the push step in CI for a few transient registry errors, e.g., retry on 5xx with exponential backoff. Saves a few noisy incidents.
build-bot: rerun started...
build-bot: rerun finished — stage=push status=SUCCEEDED :tada:
maria: nice, push succeeded on retry. Looks like a transient registry outage on that shard. I'll still open a small PR with a retry wrapper and a note in runbook about clearing builder cache if this becomes recurring.
sara: please also add a line in the incident runbook: "if push 5xx persists, try no-cache build and clear buildkit cache on builder nodes" :thumbsup:
maria: opened PR #789 adding `--retry 3` and a fallback to `skopeo copy` on manifest push errors. Marking this thread resolved for now.
